title: Quotient of a regular ring by an element with a unit derivative is regular
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], i.e. Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a regular local ring for every prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $f\in R$ and let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) such that the image of $D(f)$ in $R/fR$ is a unit. Then $R/fR$ is a regular ring (if $f$ is a unit, $R/fR=0$, which has no primes and is regular).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular, line 11798) and its proof (reduction to R local; f not in m^2 by the Leibniz rule; Algebra Lemma Tag 00NQ lemma-regular-ring-CM)
